fit.gap_handling_summary: The CV presents strong transferable AWS, Terraform, platform design, observability and technical leadership evidence without fabricating Terragrunt, TLS, certificate management or fleet experience. Terraform and general stakeholder work are appropriate adjacent evidence, but neither document directly discusses the important Terragrunt and train-to-cloud security gaps. Backend-adjacent Go/Python work is accurately presented rather than inflated into a JVM or full-stack career.

issues: The summary repeats working with product teams and leadership in consecutive sentences.
The second page is only 34.2% filled, while the first page is comparatively dense.
The current city is omitted from the contact header; this reduces logistical context but does not create an arrangement conflict.

keywords_missing_but_candidate_has: networking — some evidence through VPC and Route 53, but no demonstrated TLS specialism
virtual machines — supported by hands-on EC2 operation
reasons: Single-column text, intact extraction and conventional headings make the PDF straightforward to parse.
AWS and Terraform are backed by concrete operational scale and quantified results.
Technical leadership is expressed through the tech-lead role even though the exact phrase is not used.
Terragrunt and the train-to-cloud networking/security keywords are absent and could be decisive screening criteria.
The candidate should not add unsupported TLS, Terragrunt, IoT or JVM keywords simply to increase coverage.

issues: Company specificity is limited to the new train fleet and cloud connectivity already described in the vacancy.
Most of the letter repeats CV achievements instead of explaining how those achievements transfer to telemetry, remote updates, secure connectivity or manufacturer coordination.
It does not address the major Terragrunt and TLS/certificate-management gaps or provide a bounded explanation of the candidate's adjacent experience.
The final sentence is a long list of capabilities rather than a particularly memorable conclusion.
strengths: Names the correct company and exact contractor role.
Uses the current Tallybrook position correctly and places Brightwater in the past.
Selects strong AWS, Terraform, developer enablement and SLO examples with supported metrics.
Shows leadership through agreement with product leadership rather than implying line management.
Does not invent contractor availability, relocation, work rights in Poland or fleet-specific experience.

spacing_issues: The CV is unbalanced: page one contains all three jobs and is dense, while page two contains only additional experience, education, certifications and languages and is 34.2% filled.
Large unused space below the second CV page's language section makes the document look less deliberately balanced.
issues: A more balanced page break or modest redistribution of content would improve the CV without shrinking the readable 11-point body.
The cover letter is a clean single page with normal paragraph spacing; its lower-page whitespace is acceptable.

fluency_and_tone_issues: CV: “stakeholder engagement with product teams and leadership” is followed by “while working with product teams and leadership”; remove the repeated idea.
Letter: “brings together the infrastructure design and observability that I would bring to the role” repeats “bring” and makes the opening less direct.

Letter: “hands-on infrastructure engineering experience, AWS cloud environment design and operation, Terraform-based delivery, technical leadership and stakeholder engagement” is a cumbersome closing list.

notes_facts_used: Mentored three engineers moving from backend into SRE.
Presented the 2024 UK DevOps meetup talk “SLOs that product managers care about”.
Retained Senior Platform Engineer as the formal title and described tech lead as a responsibility, without claiming line management.
Omitted the expired CKAD as explicitly instructed.

evaluation.summary: These are accurate, readable documents that present substantial AWS, Terraform, platform engineering and technical leadership experience with well-supported metrics. The CV makes good use of portfolio and notes material without inflating the formal title, open-source work or certifications. The main application weakness is limited treatment of Terragrunt and secure train-to-cloud networking, where the supplied candidate material does not establish the requested experience. The letter is correctly targeted but largely repeats the CV, and the CV's dense first page and lightly filled second page would benefit from rebalancing.
